question: In Villafranca di Verona, a landfill for the disposal of hazardous waste containing asbestos is currently in the authorisation phase. The landfill in question is situated in an underground aquifer recharge area that is surrounded in all directions by storage sites for special and hazardous urban waste.

Given that the state of the environment in Villafranca is already very fragile and the potential impact that the facility could have both in the construction phase and in the operation and after-care management phases, the local municipality considers that building a landfill for the disposal of waste containing asbestos near Caluri and the airport runway poses a serious risk to citizens’ health.
In view of this, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Is the positioning of an asbestos landfill in an underground aquifer recharge area in line with Directive 1999/31/EC?

Does it not consider that building such a landfill in a town already suffering from environmental damage runs counter to the objectives of the directive with regard to environmental protection and rehabilitation?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.6.2024) 1. An asbestos landfill in an underground aquifer recharge area shall comply with the strict requirements of the Landfill Directive1, including the types of waste allowed to be landfilled in accordance with the particular landfill permit and the criteria and procedures for acceptance of waste in landfills2.

Landfills shall be sited, designed, constructed and operated to prevent pollution of surface water, groundwater and air. Control and monitoring shall be carried according to detailed requirements3. Specific rules apply to landfills receiving asbestos waste to ensure safe disposal, including containment, e.g., via use of binders or packaging with the aim of zero emission of asbestos fibres4.
Without prejudice to the Commission’s powers as guardian of the Treaties, Member States are primarily responsible to ensure that EU legislation is properly implemented5. 2.

A landfill permit may only be issued by the competent authority if the landfill complies with the requirements of the Landfill Directive, including its location which must take into consideration the distances from the boundary of the site to residential and recreation areas, waterways, water bodies and other agricultural or urban sites; the existence of groundwater, coastal water or nature protection zones in the area; the geological and hydrogeological conditions in the area; the risk of flooding, subsidence, landslides or avalanches on the site; and the protection of the nature or cultural patrimony in the area.

The landfill can be authorised only if the characteristics of the site with respect to these requirements, or the corrective measures to be taken, indicate that the landfill does not pose a serious environmental risk6.
1 Council Directive 1999/31/EC of 26 April 1999 on the landfill of waste, OJ L 182, 16.7.1999, p. 1–19,

amended by Directive (EU) 2018/850 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 May 2018, OJ L 150, 14.6.2018, p. 100–108. 2 Waste Acceptance criteria decision, 2003/33/EC: Council Decision of 19 December 2002 establishing criteria and procedures for the acceptance of waste at landfills pursuant to Article 16 of and Annex II to Directive 1999/31/EC, OJ L 11, 16.1.2003, p. 27–49.

3 Annex III to the Landfill Directive. 4 Section 2.3.3 of the Waste Acceptance criteria decision. 5 In line with its strategic approach on enforcement action the Commission focuses on systemic non-compliance, as set out in the Communication of 19 January 2017: EU law: Better results through better application C/2016/8600, OJ C 18, 19.1.2017, p.
10–20 and in the Communication of 13 October 2022: COM(2022) 518 final - Enforcing EU law for a Europe that delivers. 6 Article 8 and Annex I to the Landfill Directive.
